subject: ela
intro: A complete sentence has a subject (who or what) and a verb (the action), and it expresses a full thought. In formal situations (like a class presentation) we use complete, polite sentences; with friends we can be more casual. Third graders speak in complete sentences and know when to be formal.

items.prompt: Which is a COMPLETE sentence: 'Ran fast' or 'The dog ran fast'?

steps: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb and a full thought.
'The dog ran fast' has the subject 'dog' and verb 'ran.'
So that is the complete sentence.

items.prompt: In a class presentation (a formal setting), which is better: 'Yeah, it's cool' or 'Yes, it is interesting'?

steps: Formal settings use complete, polite sentences.
'Yes, it is interesting' is more formal.
So that is better for a presentation.

items.prompt: Why is 'Went to the park' NOT a complete sentence?

steps: A complete sentence needs a subject.
'Went to the park' has no subject (who went?).
So it is incomplete because it is missing the subject.
solution.answer: It is missing a subject (who went?).
